newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares shed 1.1pct, pulled down by industrials.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares shed 1.1pct, pulled down by industrials.

text.p: Despite last minute buying which limited overall losses, Greek equities lost 1.1 percent on Wednesday pulled down by industrials which stayed on the rack and had a knock-on effect on the broader market.
Brokers said the index's retreat did not depict precisely the market's true value and potential due to thin turnover.

"Current trade patterns do not give a realistic view of the market's potential and underlying value, because trading volume is light but the lack of depth is disguised behind book-entry block trades," said Dimitrios Paparistidis, broker at Kappa Securities.
Today's dealing was dominated by concentrated profit-taking in a few large caps, primarily OTE telecom, which constitute a major drag on the benchmark index, he added.
But despite easing prices buying interest was apparent on both sides of the market, especially on stocks with upbeat interim performance.
The Athens general index shed 1.10 percent or 17.46 points to 1,572.87 from Tuesday's 1,590.33 close, lifted by late minute buying from a 1,566.21 low.
